title.en: Florida sues OpenAI and Sam Altman in first US state lawsuit against an AI company over safety
title.zhHans: 佛罗里达起诉 OpenAI 和 Sam Altman，美国首次州级诉讼针对 AI 公司安全

searchSummary.en: Florida sued OpenAI and Sam Altman in 2026 — the first US state-level lawsuit against an AI company over safety. How legal accountability for AI harm reached a new frontier.
searchSummary.zhHans: 佛罗里达 2026 年起诉 OpenAI 和 Sam Altman——美国首次州级诉讼针对 AI 公司的安全问题。AI 损害的法律责任如何达到了新前沿。

summary.en: On June 1, 2026, Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, accusing the company of putting profit over safety and marketing ChatGPT as safe for children despite known risks. The suit, the first by a US state against an AI company over safety, alleged that OpenAI failed to warn users about ChatGPT's dangers. It marked a new phase in AI liability litigation, shifting from copyright disputes (NYT, Getty) to direct safety and consumer protection claims.
summary.zhHans: 2026 年 6 月 1 日，佛罗里达州总检察长 James Uthmeier 对 OpenAI 及 CEO Sam Altman 提起诉讼，指控该公司将利润置于安全之上，并在明知风险的情况下将 ChatGPT 宣传为对儿童安全的产品。这是美国州级政府首次就安全问题起诉 AI 公司，指控 OpenAI 未能警告用户 ChatGPT 的危险性。这标志着 AI 责任诉讼进入新阶段——从版权纠纷（NYT、Getty）转向直接的安全和消费者保护索赔。

narrative.en: The Florida lawsuit represented a significant escalation in the legal challenges facing AI companies. Previous major lawsuits had focused on copyright (NYT v. OpenAI, record labels v. Suno/Udio) or had been brought by individuals. Florida's suit was the first time a US state government had directly sued an AI company over safety and consumer protection. The complaint alleged that OpenAI: misled users about ChatGPT's safety, particularly for children; failed to warn users about risks including emotional dependence, harmful content, and misinformation; prioritized rapid deployment over safety testing; and engaged in deceptive trade practices by marketing ChatGPT as 'safe' and 'beneficial.' The lawsuit sought injunctive relief, civil penalties, and disgorgement of profits. The case was filed in Florida state court, not federal court, which meant it would be decided under Florida's consumer protection laws rather than federal jurisprudence. This was a strategic choice: state consumer protection laws often provide stronger remedies than federal law. The lawsuit was covered extensively as a potential watershed moment for AI regulation. Supporters argued that state-level enforcement was necessary given congressional inaction. Critics (including many in the tech industry) argued that the suit was politically motivated and could chill beneficial AI development. The case was expected to take years to resolve, but its mere filing had immediate effects: other state attorneys general began announcing their own investigations, and AI companies accelerated their trust and safety investments. The Florida lawsuit was widely seen as the AI industry's 'tobacco moment' — the first major government action that could lead to industry-wide liability.
narrative.zhHans: 佛罗里达诉讼代表了 AI 公司面临的法律挑战的重大升级。之前的主要诉讼集中在版权（NYT 诉 OpenAI、唱片公司诉 Suno/Udio）或由个人提起。佛罗里达的诉讼是首次美国州政府直接就安全和消费者保护问题起诉 AI 公司。诉状指控 OpenAI：在 ChatGPT 的安全性方面误导用户，尤其是对儿童；未能警告用户包括情感依赖、有害内容和错误信息在内的风险；将快速部署置于安全测试之上；以及通过将 ChatGPT 宣传为"安全"和"有益"而从事欺骗性商业行为。该诉讼寻求禁令救济、民事罚款和追缴利润。该案在佛罗里达州法院而非联邦法院提起，这意味着它将根据佛罗里达的消费者保护法而非联邦判例法裁决。这是一个战略选择：州消费者保护法通常比联邦法提供更强有力的救济。该诉讼被广泛报道为 AI 监管的潜在分水岭时刻。支持者认为鉴于国会不作为，州级执法是必要的。批评者（包括科技行业的许多人）认为该诉讼出于政治动机，可能阻碍有益的 AI 发展。该案预计需要数年才能解决，但其立案本身就产生了即时影响：其他州总检察长开始宣布自己的调查，AI 公司加快了信任与安全投资。佛罗里达诉讼被广泛视为 AI 行业的"烟草时刻"——可能导致全行业责任的首次重大政府行动。

description.en: First US state government lawsuit against an AI company over safety. Alleged OpenAI misled users about safety, failed to warn about risks, and marketed ChatGPT as safe for children. Sought injunctive relief, civil penalties, and disgorgement of profits. Triggered investigations by other state AGs.
description.zhHans: 美国州政府首次就安全问题起诉 AI 公司。指控 OpenAI 在安全方面误导用户，未能警告风险，并将 ChatGPT 宣传为对儿童安全。寻求禁令救济、民事罚款和追缴利润。触发了其他州总检察长的调查。

description.en: Shifted AI litigation from copyright to consumer protection and safety. Established state AGs as key AI regulators. Created precedent for state-level AI enforcement. Potentially the 'tobacco moment' for the AI industry.
description.zhHans: 将 AI 诉讼从版权转向消费者保护和安全领域。确定了州总检察长作为关键 AI 监管者的角色。为州级 AI 执法创造了先例。可能是 AI 行业的"烟草时刻"。

text.en: Florida Attorney General filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman on June 1, 2026 — the first US state lawsuit against an AI company over safety, alleging profit-over-safety conduct.
text.zhHans: 佛罗里达州总检察长于 2026 年 6 月 1 日对 OpenAI 和 Sam Altman 提起诉讼——美国首次州级诉讼针对 AI 公司安全，指控其将利润置于安全之上的行为。

text.en: Legal scholars debate whether Florida's lawsuit can succeed under Section 230 and existing First Amendment protections. Some argue the state is testing novel legal theories with uncertain precedent.
text.zhHans: 法律学者对佛罗里达的诉讼能否在 Section 230 和现有第一修正案保护下胜诉存在争议。一些人认为该州正在测试具有不确定判例的新法律理论。
